claims.statement: A compliant electronic CMR is legally equivalent to paper in Poland, but the protocol requires authentication, integrity, authorized access and agreed operating procedures.

The sidecar can avoid eFTI certification only if it does not serve as the platform used to submit regulatory information electronically to authorities; that boundary needs counsel and product controls.
There is direct operational evidence that at least one forwarder conditions the start of a 45-day payment clock on a complete invoice plus CMR/POD packet and can extend payment for missing documents.
Factoring also uses proof of completed delivery: Factris explicitly cites a CMR receipt for transport invoices and conditions one-day funding on complete documentation.
Poland supplies a large recurring road-freight base, but tonne-kilometres cannot be converted into addressable checks or revenue without shipment-count and customer-mix data.
Late payment is a widespread EU business problem, but available public evidence does not quantify how often freight payment delay is caused primarily by evidence defects.
Dashdoc already supports signed eCMR, attachments, partner sharing and rapid invoicing, so a carrier-facing document workspace is not differentiated.
Transporeon already performs payment-ready invoice verification and dispute workflow with native transport data, making a cross-system or factor-specific wedge essential.
Published TMS price ranges demonstrate software budget, but no reviewed source establishes willingness to add 4-10 PLN per shipment for this sidecar.
No reviewed source establishes that a factor or Polish TMS will distribute, integrate or revenue-share with the proposed product.
A high-margin repeat model is possible only after one mapping supports large recurring volume with few manual exceptions; actual exception rates and integration cost are unknown.

No direct evidence reviewed establishes illegality, unobtainable essential rights, mathematically impossible conservative economics or a non-delegable founder incompatibility for the bounded sidecar model.

contrary_evidence: Dashdoc already covers eCMR creation, signatures, attachments, sharing and invoicing.
Transporeon already offers payment-ready freight audit and dispute management using native platform data.
Factris directly accepts CMR receipts, so a factor may improve its own rules instead of buying a separate score.
Broad late-payment data does not show that document defects are a large enough causal wedge.
Certification becomes mandatory if the product is used for electronic regulatory submissions to authorities.
Published TMS pricing is much broader product value and cannot validate the proposed per-check price.
